source.document: seed base: stand-in rule (common movement-control practice, to confirm with the instructors)
source.quote: A bridge may only be crossed by vehicles whose military load class does not exceed the bridge classification. An unclassified bridge is not used until reconnoitred.

explanation: A bridge is crossed only if its load class is at least the column's (MLC).

source.document: seed base: stand-in rule (common movement-control practice, to confirm with the instructors)
source.quote: Posted gross weight restrictions must be respected; no posted limit means no restriction.

explanation: Posted weight limits are respected.

source.document: seed base: stand-in rule (common movement-control practice, to confirm with the instructors)
source.quote: Tunnels and underpasses need at least 0.3 m vertical clearance above the tallest vehicle.

explanation: Tunnels need 0.3 m of clearance above the tallest vehicle.

source.document: seed base: stand-in rule (common movement-control practice, to confirm with the instructors)
source.quote: Carriageway must be at least 0.5 m wider than the widest vehicle.

explanation: The carriageway is at least 0.5 m wider than the widest vehicle.

source.document: seed base: stand-in rule (common movement-control practice, to confirm with the instructors)
source.quote: Gradients must stay within the climbing capability of the least capable vehicle.

explanation: Slopes stay within the climbing capability of the column.

source.document: seed base: stand-in rule (common movement-control practice, to confirm with the instructors)
source.quote: Heavy wheeled vehicles shall not use unpaved tracks.

explanation: Heavy wheeled vehicles stay off unpaved tracks.

source.document: seed base: stand-in rule (common movement-control practice, to confirm with the instructors)
source.quote: Roads reported closed or destroyed shall not be used.

explanation: Roads believed closed (probability 0.5 or more) are not used.

source.document: seed base: stand-in rule (common movement-control practice, to confirm with the instructors)
source.quote: Routes shall not cross areas assessed as high threat.

explanation: No route crosses a high-threat area (threat level 0.8 or more).

source.document: seed base: stand-in rule (common movement-control practice, to confirm with the instructors)
source.quote: Convoys carrying fuel or ammunition shall not use tunnels.

explanation: Fuel and ammunition stay out of tunnels.

source.document: seed base: stand-in rule (common movement-control practice, to confirm with the instructors)
source.quote: Avoid built-up areas to limit interference with civilian traffic and exposure.

explanation: Built-up areas are avoided where possible (objective builtup).

source.document: seed base: stand-in rule (common movement-control practice, to confirm with the instructors)
source.quote: Dangerous goods convoys should bypass built-up areas.

explanation: Dangerous goods bypass built-up areas where possible (objective hazmat_builtup).

source.document: seed base: stand-in rule (common movement-control practice, to confirm with the instructors)
source.quote: Avoid chokepoints where a single event would block the route. Each main supply route (MSR) needs at least one alternate supply route (ASR) that is mostly disjoint.

explanation: Each group keeps a designated route after the loss of any single critical element, where the road network allows it.

source.document: seed base: stand-in rule (common movement-control practice, to confirm with the instructors)
source.quote: Prefer gentle gradients for heavy vehicles (fuel use, speed, safety).

explanation: Heavy columns prefer slopes under 8 % (objective preferences).

source.document: seed base: stand-in rule (common movement-control practice, to confirm with the instructors)
source.quote: Prefer major roads, which have the width and pavement strength for military traffic.

explanation: Medium and heavy columns prefer major roads (objective preferences).

source.document: seed base: stand-in rule (common movement-control practice, to confirm with the instructors)
source.quote: Minimise exposure to assessed threats.

explanation: Exposure to assessed threats is minimised (objective threat_exposure).

source.document: seed base: stand-in rule (common movement-control practice, to confirm with the instructors)
source.quote: By day, prefer roads under cover to reduce air observation.

explanation: By day, roads under cover are preferred (objective cover).

source.document: seed base: stand-in rule (common movement-control practice, to confirm with the instructors)
source.quote: Avoid roads degraded by weather.

explanation: Weather-degraded roads are slower (travel time) and lower the route type to Y.

source.document: seed base: stand-in rule (common movement-control practice, to confirm with the instructors)
source.quote: Each main supply route (MSR) needs at least one alternate supply route (ASR) that is mostly disjoint.

explanation: An alternate route takes at most 1.8 times the main route's travel time.

source.document: seed base: stand-in rule (common movement-control practice, to confirm with the instructors)
source.quote: Successive convoys on the same road keep a minimum time gap.

explanation: Columns on the same road in the same direction keep a 10-minute time gap.

source.document: seed base: stand-in rule (common movement-control practice, to confirm with the instructors)
source.quote: Convoy march speed is capped.

explanation: March speed at most 60 km/h.

source.document: seed base: stand-in rule (common movement-control practice, to confirm with the instructors)
source.quote: Heavy convoys march at a lower speed.

explanation: Heavy columns march at 50 km/h at most.

source.document: seed base: stand-in rule (common movement-control practice, to confirm with the instructors)
source.quote: Night (blackout) driving reduces march speed.

explanation: At night the march speed is reduced by 30 %.

source.document: seed base: stand-in rule (common movement-control practice, to confirm with the instructors)
source.quote: Scheduled halts for maintenance and crew rest.

explanation: A halt area is reached at least every 2 hours of driving.

source.document: seed base: stand-in rule (common movement-control practice, to confirm with the instructors)
source.quote: Scheduled halts for maintenance and crew rest.

explanation: Halts last 15 minutes and take place at halt areas, within their capacity.

source.document: seed base: template default value (assumption, to confirm with the instructors)

explanation: Columns with vehicles of 15 m or more take no turn sharper than 120 degrees.

source.document: seed base: template default value (assumption, to confirm with the instructors)

explanation: A dangerous goods convoy crosses at most one built-up area where an alternative exists.

source.document: seed base: template default value (assumption, to confirm with the instructors)

explanation: Start points, via-points and prohibited areas from the order are respected.

source.document: seed base: template default value (assumption, to confirm with the instructors)

explanation: At most 300 km between fuel points.

source.document: seed base: template default value (assumption, to confirm with the instructors)

explanation: Main routes of different groups do not use a narrow road in opposite directions where an alternative exists.

source.document: seed base: template default value (assumption, to confirm with the instructors)

explanation: A lateral link between a main route and its alternate at least every 10 km.

source.document: seed base: template default value (assumption, to confirm with the instructors)

explanation: Traffic control posts at critical elements, at splits and merges of designated routes, and at least every 15 km.

source.document: seed base: template default value (assumption, to confirm with the instructors)

explanation: The designated network is kept small (objective network_size).

source.document: seed base: template default value (assumption, to confirm with the instructors)

explanation: Routes used by heavy or dangerous-goods groups are dispatch routes; other designated routes are supervised; alternates are reserved.

source.document: seed base: template default value (assumption, to confirm with the instructors)

explanation: Columns do not transit built-up areas between 07:30 and 09:00 where possible.

source.document: seed base: template default value (assumption, to confirm with the instructors)

explanation: Successive rotations change at least 30 % of their route or timing.

source.document: seed base: template default value (assumption, to confirm with the instructors)

explanation: No halt or wait within 800 m of a bridge or tunnel; control post where the strike probability is 0.2 or more.

source.document: seed base: template default value (assumption, to confirm with the instructors)

explanation: Vehicle interval 50 m by day and 100 m by night; march units of at most 20 vehicles.
